answer:
The project documents I have don't mention IBM or any IBM-hosted model, so I can't tell you which provider to use.

The docs do say Promptfoo supports many providers: "Promptfoo supports 60+ providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and many others:" [promptfoo/site/docs/getting-started.md]. The provider list in these docs is not exhaustive, so IBM may be on it, but I can't confirm that from this context.

For a server with an OpenAI-compatible API, the docs describe a pattern you could try: "For llamafile, vLLM, and Text Generation WebUI, keep the `openai:chat:` prefix, enter the server's model name, and set `apiBaseUrl` including `/v1`." [promptfoo/site/docs/red-team/quickstart.md]. I don't know whether IBM's endpoints work this way. If they don't, the Python provider is the documented fallback for wrapping a custom API: "Integrating proprietary or local models" [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/python.md].

To get a definite answer, check the Promptfoo provider documentation for IBM or the current provider list on the Promptfoo site.
